headline: Pakistan has secured a 25,000-tonne tuna quota from the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission for the first time and invited the Maldives to invest in tuna processing, Business Recorder reports.

card.desc: Quota could earn around $200 million in exports

caption:
Pakistan secures its first-ever tuna quota! 🐟
According to Business Recorder, Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry said Pakistan has secured a tuna quota of 25,000 metric tonnes from the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission for the first time: 15,000 tonnes of yellowfin and 10,000 tonnes of skipjack. He said the quota could generate around $200 million in export earnings. Meeting a Maldivian delegation led by Tourism and Civil Aviation Minister Mohamed Ameen, he invited the Maldives to invest in Pakistan's tuna-processing and canning industry. A high-level Pakistani delegation is due to visit the Maldives in December.
